name: 5G Hierarchy of Threats
description: FiGHT is a knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques targeting 5G network systems. Structured similarly to MITRE ATT&CK, FiGHT enumerates the techniques an adversary might use against the 5G core, RAN (radio access network), management plane, and 5G-specific protocols (e.g., HTTP/2-based service-based architecture, SUCI/SUPI handling, network slicing). FiGHT extends or specializes ATT&CK techniques where 5G-specific variations apply.
relationToCloudSecurity: 5G cores are increasingly cloud-native (containers, microservices, Kubernetes). FiGHT techniques against the 5G core often map to underlying cloud-platform attack surface — FiGHT is the most relevant framework for operators threat-modeling cloud-hosted 5G workloads.
relationToAISecurity: FiGHT does not specifically address AI-targeting techniques. AI components in 5G (e.g., AI-driven network optimization, traffic classification) would be threat-modeled with a combination of FiGHT (network plane) and ATLAS (AI/ML plane).

license.notes: Upstream LICENSE.txt combines the Apache License 2.0 text with a separate MITRE FiGHT / ATT&CK Terms of Use notice (free use with attribution). Because both texts appear in a single file, GitHub's license detector reports NOASSERTION.

lifecycle.notes: active=true per the schema's definition (this version is currently in force; nothing supersedes it) — but note the publication cadence is quiet: no upstream commits since 2025-11-14 (HEAD 097cd5f73811). MITRE has not announced end-of-life. Re-check currency before relying on it. FiGHT has NO GitHub Releases and NO tags, and the data's own version fields are largely empty strings, so there is no version identifier to cite; pin by commit SHA.

extraction_history.reason: Removed committed fight.yaml (624 KB) and fight.json (782 KB) in favour of reference-only. The committed YAML had drifted against upstream's 1.14 MB and was missing the entire campaigns section (SolarWinds Compromise, Operation Soft Cell).

Restored as a SHA-pinned snapshot rather than a bare pointer. FiGHT publishes no release tags or versioned distributions (only an untagged branch inside a built Nuxt website repo), and convert_fight.py also produces fight.json. Fetched fresh at commit 097cd5f73811 (1.14 MB, campaigns section intact) rather than restoring the stale file.

scope.covers: 5G network adversary techniques (core, RAN, management plane, 5G-specific protocols)
scope.upstream_caveat: The mitre/FiGHT repository is a built Nuxt static website committed to git (_nuxt/, index.html, CNAME). The data files are included in that deploy artifact rather than published as a separate dataset. There are no GitHub Releases, no tags, and no issues have ever been filed; the last commit was 2025-11-14.
scope.counts_at_pinned_commit: 15 tactics, 183 techniques, 92 mitigations, 169 data sources, 10 groups, 16 software, 2 campaigns
scope.identifier_pattern: Tactics reuse 14 ATT&CK tactic IDs verbatim (TA0001..TA0043) plus FiGHT-specific TA5001 ('Fraud'). Techniques and sub-techniques split by lineage: FGT1###[.###] are ATT&CK-aligned (113 of 183, e.g. FGT1195 = ATT&CK T1195), FGT5###[.###] are 5G-original (70 of 183; 97 of the 183 total technique entries are dotted sub-techniques). Groups mix inherited ATT&CK G#### IDs (6 of 10) with FiGHT-original FGG5### (4 of 10); software mixes inherited ATT&CK S#### IDs (8 of 16) with FiGHT-original FGS5### (8 of 16). Also FGM#### (mitigation), FGDS####[.###] (data source), and campaigns mixing reused ATT&CK IDs (C0024) with FiGHT-original (FGC5001).
scope.yaml_top_level_keys: tactics, techniques, mitigations, 'data sources' (note the space), groups, software, campaigns, case-studies

notes: Niche but valuable for 5G operators. Often consumed alongside 3GPP security specifications.

desired_end_state.notes: Changed from metadata-only/upstream-only on 2026-08-14. FiGHT publishes no release tags or versioned distributions (only an untagged built website repo on main, with empty internal version fields), and convert_fight.py generates fight.json from fight.yaml. A snapshot pinned to commit 097cd5f73811 is kept and refreshed by re-pinning the SHA.
